evidence.curator_note: Book draws 1 arc; move <1> is drawn and fully accounts for the step (no implicit hook needed because the cleavage is heterolytic). The single two-electron (double-barbed) arrow runs from the C(4)-C(5) sigma bond (the beta C-C bond) into the forming C(1)=C(4) pi bond, regenerating the neutral acetone enol and leaving the beta-carbon C(5) as a carbocation. This is the charge-migration ('i', inductive) branch of the same distonic intermediate that Eq 4.33 forms: the page draws the precursor as the localized carbocation resonance form (charge drawn on the former carbonyl carbon C(1)+, oxygen a neutral -OH, radical drawn on the gamma-carbon C(6)), obtained from the molecular ion by the gamma-H rearrangement (rH, shown at the top of the page) followed by the vertical charge-migration arrow. The detected ion is the propene radical cation, drawn as the distonic form R-CH(.)-CH2(+) (radical on C(6), + on C(5)); its resonance forms are CH3-CH(+)-CH2(.) and [CH3-CH=CH2]+. -- the arrow produces exactly the drawn distonic form. Instantiated with R = CH3, giving propene+. at m/z 42 (IE = 9.7 eV, 5%); for R = C6H5 the migration product is styrene+. at m/z 104 (IE = 8.4 eV) and becomes the base peak (100%).

Cross-linked MOD rule variables, verified against this scheme rather than asserted. IMS_4_34_rH DFS '[C]1[C]2([H]3)[C]4[C]5[C]6([C]7){=}[O+.]8>>[C]1[C.]2[C]4[C]5[C+]6([C]7)[O]8[H]3' produces the charge-migration resonance form used here as the precursor: gamma-H(3) migrates to oxygen, but the product localizes the positive charge on the former carbonyl carbon C(6) (written [C+]) with a NEUTRAL hydroxyl O(8)-H(3) and the radical on the gamma-carbon C(2) -- exactly the [C+](-OH) form drawn at the bottom-left of the page (C6/C1 = carbonyl carbon, C2/C6 = gamma-carbon). IMS_4_34_ind DFS '[C]1[C.]2[C]3[C]4[C+]5([C]6)[O]7[H]8>>[C]1[C.]2[C+]3.[C]4{=}[C]5([C]6)[O]7[H]8' matches the inductive step: the beta C(3)-C(4) sigma bond cleaves heterolytically toward the carbocation, the C(4)=C(5) enol double bond forms (neutral acetone enol), the beta-carbon C(3) becomes the cation and the gamma-carbon C(2) keeps its radical -- the distonic alkene radical cation. Mapping: their C4/C5 (alpha-carbon / carbonyl carbon) = my C4/C1 forming the C(1)=C(4) pi bond, their C3 (beta-carbon) = my C5 becoming the cation. Both rules survive the L->R conservation guardrail (radical count 1 preserved throughout).
